Create an animated, interactive bar chart race.

Source: R/barChartRace.R
bar_chart_race.Rd

Ranks items (countries, products, teams...) by a value and animates the ranking through time: the bars glide past each other when they overtake, new items slide up from below the cut and leaving ones sink and fade, the value labels count smoothly, the axis follows the leader and a big period label sits in the corner. A player at the bottom plays, pauses and scrubs the animation.

Usage

bar_chart_race(
  data,
  x,
  y,
  time,
  ease = "Linear",
  frame_dur = 0,
  transition_dur = 1000,
  color_category = NULL,
  sort = "descending",
  padding_width = 0.2,
  x_font_size = 10,
  y_font_size = 12,
  x_ticks = NULL,
  x_title = NULL,
  x_title_font_size = 12,
  y_title = NULL,
  y_title_font_size = 12,
  title = NULL,
  title_font_size = 20,
  stroke = NULL,
  stroke_width = NULL,
  font = "Verdana, Geneva, Tahoma, sans-serif",
  bg_col = "white",
  panel_col = NULL,
  x_grid_line_col = NULL,
  opacity = 1,
  time_label = TRUE,
  time_label_opts = list(size = NULL, prefix = "", suffix = "", xOffset = 0, yOffset = 0),
  width = NULL,
  height = NULL,
  top_n = 10,
  group = NULL,
  fill = NULL,
  highlight = NULL,
  labels = TRUE,
  name_position = c("left", "inside"),
  total = FALSE,
  rank_flash = TRUE,
  agg = c("sum", "mean", "max", "min", "last"),
  corner_radius = 3,
  controls = TRUE,
  autoplay = TRUE,
  loop = FALSE,
  start_frame = "first",
  time_format = NULL,
  subtitle = NULL,
  subtitle_font_size = 13,
  value_format = NULL,
  value_prefix = "",
  value_suffix = "",
  tooltip = TRUE,
  axis_col = "#333333"
)

Arguments

data

The data frame containing the variables to consider (one row per item and period).

x

The name of the numeric column giving the length of the bars.

y

The name of the column giving the items (one bar per value).

time

The name of the column giving the periods: numeric (e.g. years), Date, POSIXct, or a factor or character column (factor levels, or the sorted values, give the order).

ease

The easing used within each period, a d3-ease name such as "Linear" (default, a steady race), "CubicInOut" (slows down on every period) or "BackInOut" (a little bounce). See <https://github.com/d3/d3-ease>.

frame_dur

The time, in milliseconds, the race pauses on each period before moving to the next one. Defaults to 0 (no pause). Each period lasts frame_dur + transition_dur milliseconds at 1x speed: the bars rest for frame_dur, then move for transition_dur.

transition_dur

The time, in milliseconds, spent moving from one period to the next. Defaults to 1000.

color_category

Optional. The name of a D3 categorical colour scheme (e.g. "Accent", "Tableau10", "Set2"), see <https://github.com/d3/d3-scale-chromatic#categorical>. When NULL (default), the ddplot palette is used. fill takes precedence.

sort

How the bars are ranked: "descending" (default, the largest value on top), "ascending" (the smallest value on top) or "none" (the bars keep the order of the data, or of the factor levels of y, and only the first top_n items are shown).

padding_width

The space between bars, as a share of the row height, from 0 to 0.99. Defaults to 0.2.

x_font_size

The font size of the value axis labels. Defaults to 10.

y_font_size

The font size of the item names (shrunk when the bars are thin). Defaults to 12.

x_ticks

Optional. The approximate number of value axis ticks.

x_title

Optional. The title of the value axis, drawn above it. It is also used as the name of the value in the tooltip.

x_title_font_size

The font size of the value axis title. Defaults to 12.

y_title

Optional. The title of the item names, drawn above them.

y_title_font_size

The font size of the item axis title. Defaults to 12.

title

Optional. The title of the plot.

title_font_size

The font size of the plot title. Defaults to 20.

stroke

Optional. The stroke colour of the bars.

stroke_width

Optional. The stroke width of the bars (1 when only stroke is given).

font

The font family to consider for the titles. Defaults to "Verdana, Geneva, Tahoma, sans-serif".

bg_col

The background colour of the SVG. Defaults to "white".

panel_col

Optional. The background colour of the panel behind the bars (none by default).

x_grid_line_col

The colour of the vertical grid lines. When NULL (default), a light grey, or white when panel_col is given. Use NA to hide them.

opacity

The opacity of the bars (from 0 to 1). Defaults to 1.

time_label

Logical. Show the big period label in the bottom right corner. Defaults to TRUE.

time_label_opts

A list of options for the period label: size (font size in pixels, chosen from the chart size when NULL), prefix and suffix (text around the period), xOffset and yOffset (shifts to the left and upwards, as a share of the width and height of the label, from the bottom right corner of the panel; both default to 0). Missing entries keep their defaults.

width

Optional. The width of the SVG output.

height

Optional. The height of the SVG output.

top_n

The number of bars shown. Defaults to 10 (or the number of items, when there are fewer).

group

Optional. The name of a column grouping the items (e.g. the continent of each country). The bars are coloured by group, with a clickable legend.

fill

Optional. The colours of the bars: a single colour, an unnamed vector (recycled over the items, or the groups with group), or a named vector mapping items (or groups) to colours, the others taking the palette.

highlight

Optional. A character vector of items followed from the start (the other bars are dimmed, see Interactions).

labels

Logical. Show the value at the end of each bar, counting smoothly between periods. Defaults to TRUE.

name_position

Where the item names go: "left" (default, in a column left of the bars) or "inside" (inside the end of the bar, or just after it when the bar is too short).

total

Show the total of all the items under the period label, and the share of the total in the tooltip: FALSE (default), TRUE or a label such as "World". Only meaningful for values that add up.

rank_flash

Logical. Flash a small arrow next to a bar that overtakes another one. Defaults to TRUE.

agg

How rows with the same item and period are combined: "sum" (default), "mean", "max", "min" or "last".

corner_radius

The radius of the rounded bar ends, in pixels. Defaults to 3; use 0 for square bars.

controls

Logical. Show the player (play / pause, timeline, speed, loop) and the ranking length buttons. Defaults to TRUE.

autoplay

Logical. Start playing when the chart scrolls into view. Defaults to TRUE.

loop

Logical. Start again at the end. Defaults to FALSE; it can be toggled from the player.

start_frame

The period shown first: "first" (default), "last" or a period number.

time_format

Optional. A d3-time-format string for date periods, e.g. "%b %Y". Chosen from the spacing of the dates when NULL.

subtitle

Optional. A subtitle drawn under the title.

subtitle_font_size

The font size of the subtitle. Defaults to 13.

value_format

Optional. A d3-format string for the values, e.g. ",.0f", ".1f" or ".3~s".

value_prefix, value_suffix

Optional. Text added before or after every value, e.g. "$" or " years".

tooltip

Logical. Show a tooltip on hover. Defaults to TRUE.

axis_col

The colour of the axes, labels and titles. Defaults to "#333333".

Value

An animated, interactive SVG bar chart race (an r2d3 htmlwidget).

Details

The data is long: one row per item and period, with the item names in y, the values in x and the periods in time (numbers such as years, dates, or a factor or character column whose levels give the order). Gaps inside an item are interpolated; items missing before their first or after their last period enter and leave the race.

Interactions

  • The player at the bottom plays and pauses the race (also with the space bar), the timeline can be dragged or clicked, the arrow keys step one period, Home and End jump to the start and the end. The speed button cycles from 0.5x to 4x, the loop button repeats the race.

  • Hover a bar to see its value, its rank, its change over the last period and (with total) its share of the total. The tooltip keeps updating while the race plays.

  • Click a bar to follow it: it stays highlighted, the others are dimmed, and when it falls out of the top top_n it is still shown under the cut with its rank. Click it again, or press Escape, to stop following. highlight follows items from the start.

  • With group, click a legend entry to hide or show a group (the ranks are recomputed without it), double-click it to isolate it, hover it to highlight its bars.

  • When there are more items than top_n, the buttons at the top right switch between the top top_n and a longer ranking.

  • A small green arrow flashes next to a bar that overtakes another (rank_flash).

Shiny

Inside Shiny, with r2d3::d3Output("id") and r2d3::renderD3(), clicking a bar sets input$id_clicked to a list with the item, its group, value, rank, period and whether it is now followed; input$id_frame gives the period shown (index and label). The current time, the speed, the followed items, the hidden groups and the ranking length are kept when the chart is re-rendered.

Examples

library(gapminder)
library(dplyr)
# let's select a set of countries only
gapminder <- gapminder %>%
filter(
country %in% c("Algeria", "Mexico", "Iceland", "Greece", "Finland")
)

bar_chart_race(
data = gapminder,
x = "lifeExp",
y = "country",
time = "year",
y_title = "Country",
x_title = "Life expectancy",
title = "Bar chart race of countries life expectancy"
)



# Every country, the top 10 coloured by continent, following France
bar_chart_race(
  data = gapminder::gapminder,
  x = "pop",
  y = "country",
  time = "year",
  group = "continent",
  highlight = "France",
  total = "World",
  title = "The most populous countries",
  subtitle = "Population, 1952 to 2007"
)



# Monthly dates, names inside the bars
set.seed(1)
months <- seq(as.Date("2023-01-01"), by = "month", length.out = 12)
sales <- data.frame(
  brand = rep(c("Alpha", "Bravo", "Comet", "Delta", "Echo", "Fusion"), 12),
  month = rep(months, each = 6),
  units = round(runif(72, 20, 80))
)
sales$units <- ave(sales$units, sales$brand, FUN = cumsum)
bar_chart_race(
  sales, x = "units", y = "brand", time = "month",
  name_position = "inside", ease = "CubicInOut",
  value_suffix = " units", title = "Units sold, year to date"
)
